**Short version:** The three passages are rewritten below. I added no term definitions inside them. The terms that still need a definition are listed at the end.

## Passage 1

```markdown
- Block save. It applies to a run of up to 16 consecutive tokens inside one 16-token block.
  - Transpose: the K rows of the run are transposed in registers.
  - Write: the transposed rows are written as whole 64-byte lines. Each line takes one store.
  - Partial block: the store is masked when the run does not fill the block.
  - One-token run: this run keeps the scatter. Every decode step produces a one-token run.
- Sharing. The main thread and the idle main helper threads claim the blocks from one counter.
  - Helper count: the generated plugin decides the count for each pass. The count is not fixed. The traced runs used 7 helpers at tp2.
  - Calling thread only: two cases store on the calling thread.
    - single-worker callers (the handwritten plugins and the unit tests)
    - passes of at most 16 tokens
```

## Passage 2

```markdown
Rows where write keeps less than read. There are two kinds:

- two writers in one DSU at 160 KiB
- eight writers at any size

In these rows, the writers share one path. Write streams saturate that path sooner than read streams do.

Rate of one stream:

- write: 32 GB/s
- read: 9 to 12 GB/s

The shared path is one of these:

- the mesh port of one DSU
- the DRAM write ceiling (section 8)
```

## Passage 3

```markdown
Codex gave a closing assessment. The plan now states it.

The rows can show four things:

- whether the gain needs the prefetchers
- whether the prefetchers target the L3
- whether demand reads find lines in the L3
- whether more requests wait at the home nodes

The rows alone cannot distinguish two explanations:

- Your explanation: the data is already in the L3 when the core requests it.
- The alternative: the DSU handles the same prefetch requests faster.

The external-fetch count with the L3 enabled stays "Insufficient data". This holds until a counter's source and population are established on the target.

The bit-6 boot is the only intervention under consideration that acts directly on the mechanism in your explanation.
```

## Wording changes to confirm

Each change below replaces a figurative phrase with my reading of it:

- Passage 2 heading: "Where write loses instead" became "Rows where write keeps less than read".
- Passage 3: "your picture" became "your explanation".
- Passage 3: "data waiting in the L3 ahead of the core" became "the data is already in the L3 when the core requests it".
- Passage 3: "aim at" became "target".
- Passage 3: "on the table" became "under consideration".
- Passage 3: "acts on your picture" became "acts directly on the mechanism in your explanation".

## Terms that need a definition at first use

The passages are excerpts. Their parent documents may define these terms earlier. I cannot see those documents, so the parent documents are the source that resolves each row.

| Term | Passage | Status |
|---|---|---|
| K rows | 1 | Insufficient data. |
| tp2 | 1 | Insufficient data. |
| generated plugin, handwritten plugins, main helper threads | 1 | Project names. Insufficient data. |
| scatter | 1 | Reading, not verified: the scatter-store instruction of the earlier save code. |
| "keeps" | 2 | The passage does not name the quantity that is kept. |
| DSU | 2, 3 | Reading, not verified: Arm DynamIQ Shared Unit (a core cluster with a shared L3 cache). |
| mesh port | 2 | Insufficient data. |
| DRAM write ceiling | 2 | "Ceiling" is a metaphor. Keep it only if section 8 defines it. Otherwise write "maximum DRAM write rate". |
| Codex | 3 | Reading, not verified: the OpenAI coding agent that reviewed the plan. |
| home nodes | 3 | Reading, not verified: the Arm mesh nodes that serve cache-line requests. |
| external-fetch count, population | 3 | Insufficient data. |
| bit-6 boot | 3 | Insufficient data. The passage does not name the register. |

The sentence lengths were counted by hand. The check_lengths.py script was not run, because the output is not a file.
